prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t pick one single “best” for you — that depends on your neighborhood, budget, scope (one room vs whole house, trim vs walls), timeline, and whether you want extras like color consulting or wallpaper removal. I can, however, help you find the best company for your needs and tell you exactly how to evaluate bids.

If you want personalized recommendations, tell me:
- ZIP code or neighborhood in St. Louis
- Residential or commercial
- Rooms/area to be painted (sq ft or number of rooms)
- Any prep work needed (repairs, wallpaper removal, ceiling work)
- Desired start date and budget range

Until then, here’s a practical, quick plan to find the best interior painter in St. Louis and what to check for:

How to find candidates
- Search Google Maps, Yelp, Houzz, Angi (Angie’s List), and Nextdoor for highly rated local painters in your ZIP code.
- Look for companies with lots of recent reviews and photos of completed jobs.
- Ask neighbors, realtors, or contractors for referrals.

How to evaluate and compare
- Get written estimates from at least three companies.
- Verify they’re insured (general liability and workers’ comp) and ask for proof.
- Ask for local references and recent project photos similar to yours.
- Check the Better Business Bureau and read recent reviews for patterns.

Key questions to ask each painter
- Are you licensed and insured? (Ask to see certificates.)
- Who will do the work — company employees or subs?
- What prep is included (patching, sanding, priming, move furniture)?
- What brands/types of paint do you use and why?
- How many coats are included, and are ceilings/trim included?
- What is the estimated timeline and work hours?
- What’s your warranty/guarantee on workmanship and paint?
- How will you protect floors/furniture and manage cleanup?

Red flags
- Huge upfront payment requests (more than 10–20% for materials is uncommon).
- No written contract or vague scope.
- Consistently poor or very old/one-line online reviews.
- Pressure to sign immediately.

Pricing guidance (ballpark)
- Small rooms: often $300–800 each for labor and paint (varies with prep).
- Whole-home interior: commonly $2,000–10,000 depending on size/finish level.
- Per-square-foot estimates in many areas run about $1.50–3.50/ft² for walls (varies widely).
These are rough — get local written estimates.

Contract checklist
- Detailed scope (rooms, surfaces, number of coats)
- Brand and sheen of paint
- Prep and repair work included
- Start and completion dates
- Total price and payment schedule
- Cleanup and disposal terms
- Warranty terms

If you share your ZIP code and the project details, I’ll suggest 3–5 well-rated companies or write a short message you can send to painters asking for estimates.
